clue.text: Fellows scored after upsetting drink

indicators.note: the fellows' letters come after the upset word
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word for scored upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: to ace something is to score it perfectly, as with a serve in tennis
FF is the plural abbreviation of fellow, as f is of folio

explanation.surface: Members of a college order a drink after an upsetting result.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads from the bottom; the fellows' letters then sit below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaff is a decaffeinated coffee, a drink with its caffeine removed.

clue.text: Transmit over the internet stories about five players — that's about right

indicators.note: the word for stories goes around five, about meaning surrounding it

parts.note: lies are untrue stories
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the second about again means surrounding: the word for players wraps right

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Someone broadcasting yarns about a five-a-side team online, with a nervous aside that it's correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To livestream is to broadcast video live on the web as events happen.

clue.text: Rich fools about to accept dodgy myth on a regular basis

indicators.note: the rearranged rich takes in the other letters, accepting them inside
to fool about is to mess around, so the letters of rich are messed into a new order
something dodgy is unreliable or wrong, so the letters of myth are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wealthy idiots taking on board a questionable legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich fools' reads as a phrase, but 'fools about' signals a jumble of the first word, and 'dodgy' a second jumble that goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rhythmic recurs with a steady beat, happening at regular intervals.

clue.text: Leave talk, missing one truthful statement

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for one is dropped from the word for talk

parts.note: a spiel is a long, glib piece of talk
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave off the chatter, short of one honest statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel truth is something entirely reliable, so gospel is used for any statement taken as undoubtedly true.

clue.text: Lots of flowers are found in Greek territories

indicators.note: the unit for are is found inside the combined letters of Greek and territories

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for Greek
lands are territories or countries
an are is a metric unit of area, a hundred square metres, abbreviated AR

explanation.surface: Plenty of blooms grow across the lands of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlands are wreaths or loops made from many flowers woven together.

clue.text: Group taking a bit to produce special item

parts.note: a set is a group of things
a piece is a bit of something

explanation.surface: A group taking a small piece to create a unique item.
explanation.definitionFit: A set piece is a carefully arranged, showpiece passage or event, a standout item in a performance.

clue.text: Nasty leader deposed, as should be the case

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and deposing it removes it from the front

parts.note: frightful means very nasty or unpleasant

explanation.surface: A cruel ruler is overthrown, as justice demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful describes what is proper or just, the way things ought properly to be.

clue.text: Airmen soaring, circling Italy, having good weather

indicators.note: the reversed airmen go round the letter for Italy, circling it
in a down clue, soaring means going upward, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force, the airmen
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Pilots climbing high above Italy, enjoying fine conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF soaring gives FAR, which circles I.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is fine and dry, so a fair day is one with pleasant conditions.

clue.text: Money running short when raised for factory machine

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted up, so the letters run bottom to top
running short means lacking at the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: moola is slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds getting tight when a factory machine is purchased.
explanation.walkthrough: MOOLA running short is MOOL, raised it becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loom is a machine for weaving cloth, common in textile mills.

clue.text: Religious service affecting godliness? Not the first third of it

indicators.text: Not the first third of it
indicators.note: the opening three of the word's nine letters, its first third, are removed

parts.note: spiritual means concerning the soul and godliness

explanation.surface: A church ceremony that touches on piety, minus a part.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIRITUAL has nine letters; losing its first third, SPI, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a prescribed ceremony, such as a rite performed in worship.

clue.text: Urine not analysed for tiny particle

indicators.note: analysing breaks something down into parts, so the letters are taken apart and reordered

explanation.surface: A lab report: a sample of urine was not tested for a minute speck.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a subatomic particle with almost no mass and no charge.

clue.text: I find I am almost nuts, crazy for ever

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of nuts is lost

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they are nearly mad, mad for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'crazy' look like a pair of synonyms; NUT with I FIND I AM is the pool of letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad infinitum is Latin for 'to infinity', meaning endlessly or without limit.

clue.text: New promotion about part of plane cut down in next to no time

indicators.note: the word for promotion sits around the shortened part, about meaning surrounding

parts.note: an ad is an advert, a promotion

indicators.note: cut down means trimmed, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the nose cone is the pointed front section of an aircraft or rocket

explanation.surface: A fresh advert about a section of aircraft being shot down very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A nose cone is the pointed front of a rocket or aircraft; 'cut down' docks its last letter before the advert wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, so it is used for an instant.

clue.text: Fool in book almost split symbol with stave

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cleft means split or divided

explanation.surface: An idiot in a book nearly tore apart a musical symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool in book' places ASS next to B rather than truly inside it. A clef is the sign at the start of a musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass clef is the musical sign placed on a staff to fix the pitch of lower notes.

clue.text: Call up about fire in the sky

indicators.note: the reversed word sits around the pile for burning, about meaning surrounding
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: to name someone is to call them something
a pyre is a heap of wood made for a funeral fire

explanation.surface: A summons about a blaze high overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning summon, but 'up' is a separate reversal signal for the down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Empyrean as an adjective means heavenly, belonging to the highest heaven.

clue.text: Figure in geometry, German expert brought over in care of academic

indicators.note: the reversed letters are placed in the academic's keeping, inside the word

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: brought over means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A German specialist is brought across to be looked after by a lecturer, all about a geometric shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In care of' reads as a postal phrase; here it means placed inside the academic's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a polygon with ten sides and ten angles, a plane shape.

clue.text: Blogger exercised about date and name of variations

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the date's abbreviation, about meaning surrounding
exercised means worked over, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An online writer got worked up over a date and the title of a musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: Bach's Goldberg Variations are named after the harpsichordist said to have played them first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goldberg Variations is Bach's keyboard work, a set of thirty variations on an aria.

clue.text: Succeed in taking out middle of red target and shout

indicators.note: taking out means removing, so the central letter of red is removed from the word for succeed

parts.note: to excel is to succeed outstandingly

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter

parts.note: an aim is a target

explanation.surface: A marksman hits the bullseye of a red target and cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'middle of red' is the bullseye in the surface, but in the wordplay it is just the central letter of the word red.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, as in surprise or delight.

clue.text: Insulting the powerful? Not exactly seemly to include a joke

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take the other letters inside them, including them
not exactly means not in the precise form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: Mocking those in authority is hardly decorous when it contains a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: Lèse-majesté is French for injured majesty; the grid drops the accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lèse-majesté is the crime of offending a sovereign, and loosely any affront to those in power.

clue.text: Cheerful judge I found in cricket venue

indicators.note: the letter I is found inside the venue's name

parts.note: the Oval is a famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A judge in good spirits spotted at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London Test cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means good-humoured and merry, from the supposedly cheerful influence of Jupiter.

clue.text: With a couple of swaps, group of performers performs

indicators.note: two pairs of neighbouring letters trade places, the first two and the last two

parts.note: a cast is the group of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A troupe changes a couple of members and puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: In CAST, C and A trade places, as do S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform a role, so acts means performs on stage.

clue.text: Small area of land is left reduced by 50%

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is cut, so only its first two letters remain

explanation.surface: A plot of ground that has been halved.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, especially a small one surrounded by water.

clue.text: Carbon and carbonised material? Support monetary incentive

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
ash is what remains after something is burned
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A chemist's query about burnt matter, then a call for support.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashback is money refunded to a buyer as an inducement to purchase.

clue.text: Slender volume bound in steel, unexpectedly

indicators.note: the volume's letter is bound inside the rearranged letters
unexpectedly suggests things turned out differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A thin book surprisingly bound in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' is not about bookbinding here: STEEL rearranged as SELTE holds V.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slim and elegant in figure.

clue.text: Very fierce about women using bad language

indicators.note: the word for very fierce surrounds the letter for women, about meaning around

parts.note: searing means intensely fierce or burning

explanation.surface: Someone furious about women, cursing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is the use of profanity, cursing with offensive words.

clue.text: English navigator recalled wonderful feature of fish

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: fab is informal for fabulous, wonderful
a fin is a part of a fish

explanation.surface: An explorer remembered a superb part of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: William Baffin was a 17th-century English explorer of the Arctic; Baffin Island is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: William Baffin was an English seaman who charted Arctic waters seeking the Northwest Passage.
